title: Hand landmarks detection guide (MediaPipe Hand Landmarker)
summary: Official task documentation. The model bundle is a palm detector plus a hand landmark model that outputs 21 keypoints per hand, handedness, image-normalised landmarks (x, y in [0,1], z relative to the wrist) and world landmarks in metres with the origin at the hand's geometric centre. numHands defaults to 1; the three confidence thresholds default to 0.5. The page states the landmark model was trained on about 30K real-world images plus synthetic hands and lists a Pixel 6 latency of 17.12 ms (CPU) / 12.27 ms (GPU).
verificationNote: Page opened 2026-11-21 (ai.google.dev URL redirects to developers.google.com). All listed facts read from the page. The Pixel 6 latency is a phone benchmark, not a browser benchmark.

title: Hand landmarks detection guide for Web
summary: Web (JavaScript) guide for @mediapipe/tasks-vision. Web running modes are IMAGE and VIDEO only; the page says web tasks run synchronously and recommends VIDEO mode driven by requestAnimationFrame for live camera input. WASM assets are loaded with FilesetResolver.forVisionTasks; delegate "GPU" can be set in baseOptions. Handedness refers to the subject's hand, so a mirrored image inverts the labels.
verificationNote: Page opened 2026-11-21. The page does not state browser frame rates and does not describe CPU fallback behaviour.

title: MediaPipe Hands: On-device Real-time Hand Tracking
summary: Describes the two-model pipeline (palm detector, then hand landmark model) that predicts a hand skeleton from a single RGB camera and runs in real time on mobile GPUs.
verificationNote: arXiv abstract page opened 2026-11-21. Only the abstract was read; it contains no accuracy or frame-rate figures.

title: Mediapipe and CNNs for Real-Time ASL Gesture Recognition
summary: ASL alphabet (26 classes, A-Z) recognition from MediaPipe hand landmarks. Features are 21 landmarks re-centred and scaled, flattened to a 42-input network; 4,500 images per class; 80/20 train/test split. Abstract reports 99.95% accuracy.
verificationNote: arXiv abstract page and full PDF opened 2026-11-21. The abstract and conclusion say 99.95%, while the results section says 100% test accuracy and the classification report shows 1.00; the paper is internally inconsistent. The arXiv listing shows three authors; the PDF lists a fourth (S. K. Singh). The split is a random 80/20 split; signer identity is not discussed. Not peer reviewed (preprint).

title: Owo AI: asl-sign-detection-mediapipe-rf (GitHub repository)
summary: Open-source ASL fingerspelling project. 63 features (21 keypoints x 3) from MediaPipe, 28 classes (A-Z, space, del), Kaggle ASL Alphabet dataset (87,000 raw images, about 69,273 samples after landmark extraction), stratified 80/20 split. README reports XGBoost on normalised landmarks 98.43%; Random Forest 97.64% (raw) and 98.17% (normalised). Code licence MIT.
verificationNote: Repository page opened 2026-11-21. Numbers are self-reported in a README, with no paper. The README says 'normalized landmarks'; the specific phrase 'wrist-normalized' used by the legacy prototype was not confirmed in the text read.

title: Real-Time Indian Sign Language Alphabet Recognition Using MediaPipe Hand Landmarks and Random Forest Classification
venue: International Research Journal of Modernization in Engineering Technology and Science (IRJMETS), Vol. 08, Issue 06, June 2026
summary: ISL manual alphabet (26 classes, A-Z) from MediaPipe Hands landmarks. 126-D wrist-relative feature vector for up to two hands (zero-padded when one hand is present). 31,200 webcam images (1,200 per letter); landmarks detected in 29,871 (95.7%); 3x landmark augmentation to 119,484 samples; stratified 80/20 split; 300-tree Random Forest reaches 98.12% on 23,897 test samples. Lowest detection rates for H, Z, X, V; lowest F1 for C, M, N.
verificationNote: Full 10-page PDF opened and read 2026-11-21. The paper states the 80/20 split is applied to the 119,484 augmented samples, so augmented copies of one source image can fall in both train and test; the paper does not state the number of signers and does not report a signer-independent result. The paper states no formal latency profiling was performed. The dataset is not published.

title: Real-Time American Sign Language Interpretation Using Deep Learning and Keypoint Tracking
summary: ASL alphabet (26 classes) detection combining MediaPipe keypoints with a YOLOv11 detector. Dataset of 130,000 images, split 80/10/10. Reports precision 0.985, recall 0.981, mAP@0.5 0.982, mAP@0.5-0.95 0.933.
verificationNote: The MDPI URL returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching on 2026-11-21. Verified instead from the open-access PubMed Central copy of the same article (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11991612/, DOI 10.3390/s25072138), which contains the 130,000-image sentence and the Table 3 metrics. The data are stated as available on request, not public. mAP is a detection metric and is not comparable with classification accuracy.

title: American Sign Language Recognition for Alphabets Using MediaPipe and LSTM
summary: ASL alphabet recognition (26 letters) using MediaPipe hand landmarks and an LSTM on a custom dataset; abstract reports 99% accuracy.
verificationNote: Verified at abstract level only, from the authors' institutional repository page opened 2026-11-21. The ScienceDirect full text (PII S1877050922021378) was not opened, so dataset size, split and evaluation protocol are unknown. This is the probable source of the unsourced 'MediaPipe + LSTM (ASL) 99.0' bar in the legacy prototype, but the prototype gives no citation, so that link is an inference.

title: INCLUDE: A Large Scale Dataset for Indian Sign Language Recognition
venue: ACM Multimedia 2020 (MM '20), DOI 10.1145/3394171.3413528; dataset record on Zenodo
summary: Word-level ISL video dataset: 263 word signs in 15 categories, about 0.27 million frames, 4,292 videos on Zenodo (paper reports 4,287), recorded with deaf students of St. Louis School for the Deaf, Chennai. INCLUDE-50 is a 50-sign subset. Record states best model accuracy of 94.5% on INCLUDE-50 and 85.6% on INCLUDE. Licence CC BY 4.0.
verificationNote: Zenodo record opened 2026-11-21; all listed facts are from that record. The ACM paper itself was not opened. The Zenodo record does not state the number of signers; the figure of 7 signers comes from comparison tables in ref-joshi-2024-isign and ref-patra-2024-hwgat-fdmse.

title: CISLR: Corpus for Indian Sign Language Recognition
summary: Word-level ISL recognition corpus with a vocabulary of around 4,700 words. Baseline is a prototype-based one-shot learner using features learned from ASL.
verificationNote: ACL Anthology abstract page opened 2026-11-21. The abstract gives no accuracy figures and no video or signer counts; those counts (4,765 words, 7,050 videos, 71 signers) are taken from Table 1 of ref-joshi-2024-isign.

title: iSign: A Benchmark for Indian Sign Language Processing
summary: ISL-English benchmark with 118,228 video-sentence/phrase pairs (252 hours, about 40k vocabulary) sourced from YouTube ISL content (ISLRTC, ISH News, Deaf Enabled Foundation). Five tasks including translation, pose generation and word/gloss recognition. Its Table 1 compares isolated ISL datasets: CISLR 4,765 words / 7,050 videos / 71 signers; INCLUDE 263 / 4,287 / 7; ISL-CSLRT 186 / 700 / 7.
verificationNote: arXiv HTML full text opened 2026-11-21. The ACL Findings venue comes from the arXiv listing and ACL Anthology search results; the Anthology page itself was not opened. Total signer count for iSign is not stated.

title: Hierarchical Windowed Graph Attention Network and a Large Scale Dataset for Isolated Indian Sign Language Recognition
summary: Introduces FDMSE-ISL (40,033 videos, 2,002 words, 20 deaf signers, 10 male and 10 female) and a keypoint-based graph attention model (HWGAT). Uses a signer-independent split (10 train / 2 validation / 8 test signers, no overlap). Reports top-1 93.86% on FDMSE-ISL and 97.67% on INCLUDE.
verificationNote: arXiv abstract page and v2 HTML full text opened 2026-11-21. Preprint; peer-review status not checked. The paper says the INCLUDE result uses the dataset's provided partitions and does not say whether those are signer-independent.

title: OpenHands: Making Sign Language Recognition Accessible with Pose-based Pretrained Models across Languages
summary: Library and pose datasets for word-level sign recognition in six sign languages including Indian. Trains four pose-based isolated sign recognition models and reports that self-supervised pretraining on unlabelled Indian-SL pose data helps in low-resource settings.
verificationNote: arXiv abstract page opened 2026-11-21. Only the abstract was read; no accuracy figures are quoted from this source.

title: Real-time Indian Sign Language (ISL) Recognition
venue: 9th International Conference on Computing, Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT), 2018; arXiv:2108.10970
summary: Pre-MediaPipe ISL system: skin-colour segmentation, grid-based features, k-NN for 33 static hand poses and HMM chains for 12 gestures. Abstract reports 99.7% for static poses and 97.23% for gestures.
verificationNote: arXiv abstract page opened 2026-11-21. Only the abstract was read; evaluation protocol and number of signers were not checked.

title: On the Importance of Signer Overlap for Sign Language Detection
summary: Argues that benchmarks with the same signers in train and test give over-optimistic results. Removing signer overlap gave a relative accuracy decrease of 4.17% on the DGS corpus and 6.27% on Signing in the Wild; proposes partitions without signer overlap.
verificationNote: arXiv abstract page opened 2026-11-21. The task is sign language detection (is someone signing), not sign recognition, and the corpora are not ISL; it is cited for the evaluation principle only.

title: Continuous Fingerspelling Dataset for Indian Sign Language
venue: Workshop on Sign Language Processing (WSLP) at IJCNLP-AACL 2025, pages 33-38
summary: Continuous ISL fingerspelling dataset: 1,308 segments from 499 ISH News videos, 70.85 minutes, 14,814 characters. A ByT5-small baseline reaches 82.91% character error rate after fine-tuning, which shows the task is far from solved.
verificationNote: ACL Anthology page and the project page (https://kirandevraj.github.io/ISL-Fingerspelling/) opened 2026-11-21. Only the abstract was read for the results.

title: The History of ISL: Its Origin, Development and Relationship with Other Signed and Spoken Languages (Indian Sign Language course 230, Module 1, Lesson 2)
summary: Government course material. States that ISL was developed by the Indian deaf community and not borrowed from another country; that ISL two-handed fingerspelling is similar to that of British Sign Language with only minor differences such as A, E, I, O, U; that apart from fingerspelling, ISL signs differ significantly from BSL; and that International Sign and ASL influence some current ISL usage.
verificationNote: PDF pages 13-18 opened and read 2026-11-21. Educational material, not a peer-reviewed linguistic study; publication year is not printed on the pages read.

title: Indo-Pakistani Sign Language
summary: States that most signers use fingerspelling based on BSL fingerspelling, lists regional varieties (Bangalore-Madras, Bombay, Calcutta, Delhi and others), and describes non-manual features (mouth pattern, facial expression, body posture, head position, eye gaze) and the grammatical use of space.
verificationNote: First 100,000 characters of the page opened 2026-11-21. Tertiary source; signer population figures on the page carry a citation-needed tag and are not used by RTSLR.

title: Indian Sign Language Research and Training Centre (ISLRTC) official website
authors: ISLRTC, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India
summary: ISLRTC is an autonomous organisation established on 28 September 2015 under the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities. The home page links to the ISL Dictionary as a dictionary website, YouTube channel, Google Drive folder and a data.gov.in catalogue entry.
verificationNote: Home page opened 2026-11-21. The home page does not state the number of dictionary terms or any reuse licence; it only says the content is owned by ISLRTC. The linked dictionary website (connection refused) and the data.gov.in catalogue (HTTP 403) could not be opened.

title: ISL-CSLTR: Indian Sign Language Dataset for Continuous Sign Language Translation and Recognition
summary: Sentence-level ISL dataset. Search-result extracts of the record describe 700 annotated videos, 18,863 sentence-level frames and 1,036 word-level images for 100 spoken-language sentences performed by 7 signers.
verificationNote: Not verified. data.mendeley.com could not be opened from this environment on 2026-11-21 (TLS certificate chain error on every attempt). The description comes from web-search result extracts only; the licence field was not seen. The iSign paper's Table 1 independently lists 'ISL-CSLRT' as 186 words / 700 videos / 7 signers and cites Elakkiya and Natarajan (2021).
